facts.Current degree: BJMC / B.A. Journalism & Mass Communication – Sports / Business / Science Journalism

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build business news clips and apply for trainee business reporter, newsroom researcher and digital financial-content roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Choose a beat such as markets, banking, startups, technology, jobs, corporate affairs or public policy.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward senior business correspondent, investigative reporter, markets editor or industry specialist.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine financial literacy, data analysis, trusted sourcing and clear explanations of complex economic issues.

blocks.label: Timeline assumption
blocks.text: This roadmap uses 2026–2030 as a four-year planning horizon. If your bachelor’s programme is three years, complete the core reporting portfolio and internship milestones by graduation and treat the fourth-year activities as optional extensions.
These are planning outputs;

blocks.label: Four-year honours variant
blocks.text: If your institution offers a four-year honours route, use the additional time for a company or sector investigation, a data journalism project, an internship or research on business and economic communication. Confirm the actual course structure with your university.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Build a reputation for explaining what financial and economic developments mean for people, workers and businesses. Learn to read primary documents, question promotional claims, disclose uncertainty and use data tools responsibly. Over time, develop investigative, editing and team-leadership skills alongside subject expertise.

blocks.text: Confirm whether the role accepts undergraduate students, whether it is paid, and whether it requires economics, commerce or finance coursework. An internship’s title alone does not guarantee that a student journalist is eligible.

blocks.label: Job-posting note
blocks.text: Review current vacancies and track recurring requirements such as financial literacy, languages, writing tests, spreadsheet skills and experience. Do not present investment advice as reporting, and clearly distinguish verified facts from estimates or opinions.
Postgraduate study is optional for business reporting. It can help if you want to specialise in financial journalism, economics, public policy, business research or data journalism.

Career progression

items: Years 10–15: Senior Correspondent / Investigative Business Journalist
Years 20+: Editorial Director, independent journalist, consultant or journalism educator
blocks.label: Years 1–2

blocks.text: These are indicative ranges, not guaranteed promotion dates. Progress depends on reporting quality, financial literacy, original sourcing, beat expertise and editorial judgement.
PhD routes
A PhD is optional and most relevant to a research or academic career.

blocks.label: Business and financial journalism
blocks.text: Research corporate coverage, financial information and newsroom practices.

blocks.label: Economics and public policy
blocks.text: Investigate economic reporting, public spending, employment or regulation.

blocks.label: Media and communication
blocks.text: Study business news, audiences, misinformation or the influence of media on economic decisions.

blocks.label: Data journalism
blocks.text: Research data communication, statistical interpretation or digital reporting methods.
Check eligibility, supervisor availability, funding and research proposal requirements with each university.

2040–2046: staying relevant. Build a reputation for explaining complex business developments accurately and independently. Read original filings and public datasets, distinguish company claims from independently verified facts, and avoid overstating what the numbers show. Develop editing, investigation and team leadership skills as you advance.
